about: Place names the player is told (ink UI round, gen/ui/STYLE.md 'Place notifications'). region: the large banner shown when you walk into this section's region (sections sharing a region id show it once). landmarks: a vertical name plaque stands over the map entity id as you approach (江南百景圖's plaques), and a toast with the line from the painting's reading when you come within r metres of its footprint (or its point); top: the plaque's height when the map has none. Every name and line in 繁體, from the painting and its readings; src says where. Lore (round 2, gen/ui/r2_lore.md): long is the longer description under the toast's fold and in the 圖志 journal; quote and quoteSrc an exact line from a period or scholarly source; cite the sources as the player reads them; longSrc one note per claim (never shown); crop the map IDs that frame the painting's crop (tools/place_crops.mjs). Bundled for the page by tools/ui_data.mjs into web/public/assets/ui/places.json (short) and lore.json (long, fetched when needed). Every displayed field has an English sibling `<field>_en`, shown as a gloss under the Chinese when the viewer picks 中英 (Chinese stays the default).

region.name: 十字街
region.sub_en: The Busy Market Inside the City
region.src: map/sections.json S6 '城内十字街 · 闹市'; 余辉《深度游》第六段 '从城门内开始经十字路口到水井处'
region.long: 進了城門，便是畫中最熱鬧的市街。余輝說這一段從城門內經十字路口，一直到水井為止，畫家「以孫記正店為中心」。正店門前彩樓高搭，兩頂媒婆的轎子正要在門口落下；肉鋪前圍了一圈人聽說書；十字路口，騾子拉的大車急轉過街角。香藥鋪、客店、醫鋪、綢緞鋪一家挨著一家，士子、僧人、挑夫、閒人擠在同一條街上。余輝為這一段取的題目是「鬧市繁華顯不平」。
region.long_en: Inside the gate lies the liveliest market street in the painting. Yu Hui says this stretch, from just inside the gate across the crossroads to the well, is where the painter “centres on the Sun establishment's main tavern.” In front of the tavern a festive tower is raised high, and two go-between ladies' sedans are about to set down at its door; in front of the butcher's a circle of people listens to a storyteller; at the crossroads a mule-drawn cart swings sharply round the corner. Incense shops, inns, doctors' shops and silk shops stand one after another, and scholars, monks, porters and idlers all crowd the same street. Yu Hui's title for this stretch is “The Busy Market Shows Inequality Amid Its Splendour.”
region.quote_en: After long years of peace, the people were many and the goods plentiful.
region.cite: 余輝《清明上河圖深度游》・故宮名畫記・《東京夢華錄》
region.cite_en: Yu Hui, An In-Depth Tour of the Qingming Scroll · Palace Museum, Minghuaji · Dreams of Splendour of the Eastern Capital
longSrc: YH23: 第六段：闹市从城门内开始经十字路口到水井处…画家以"孙记正店"为中心

landmarks.name: 孫羊正店
landmarks.line: 京師正店之一，門首縛綵樓歡門。
landmarks.line_en: One of the capital's main taverns, with a festive gate tower.
landmarks.src: 名画记 36 孙羊家正店; 《东京梦华录》卷二 酒楼: '凡京师酒店，门首皆缚彩楼欢门', '在京正店七十二户'
landmarks.long: 這是畫中最氣派的酒樓。臨街搭起高大的彩樓歡門，綴滿花枝；門前燈箱寫著「正店」「香醪」，另一隻只認得一個「孫」字。樓上窗裏坐滿了飲酒的客人。余輝說，「正店」是官府授權釀酒的酒店，其餘的小酒家叫「腳店」，多向正店打酒來賣。門口還立著葫蘆形的紅燈，故宮名畫記說叫「梔子燈」，到了宋代成了酒店有妓女陪酒的標記。
landmarks.long_en: This is the most imposing tavern in the painting. A tall festive welcome gate of silk and flowers is raised along the street, hung all over with blossoms; the lantern boxes in front read “Main Tavern” and “Fragrant Wine,” and another shows only the character “Sun.” Guests fill the windows upstairs, drinking. Yu Hui explains that a “main tavern” was a wine house officially licensed to brew, while the smaller wine houses were called “leg taverns” and mostly bought their wine from main taverns to resell. At the door also stand red gourd-shaped lanterns, which the Palace Museum's notes call “gardenia lanterns”; by the Song they had become a sign that a tavern had women to keep drinkers company.
landmarks.quote: 在京正店七十二戶，此外不能遍數，其餘皆謂之腳店。
landmarks.quote_en: In the capital there are seventy-two main taverns, besides others too many to count; the rest are all called leg taverns.
landmarks.cite: 故宮名畫記・余輝〈十大看點〉・《東京夢華錄》・畫中所見
landmarks.cite_en: Palace Museum, Minghuaji · Yu Hui, Ten Highlights · Dreams of Splendour of the Eastern Capital · What the painting shows
longSrc: MHJ 36: 彩楼欢门上缀满了绣球、花枝…三个地灯上写着"香醪"、"正店"，另一个可以看见一个"孙"字…店内顾客盈门

landmarks.name: 孫羊店
landmarks.line_en: Lamb lungs and tripe hang on the counter.
landmarks.src: 余辉 2023《深度游》第六段: 孙羊店's offal counter and its price board (reading disputed: the map reads pork)
landmarks.long: 街角的肉鋪掛著一面白布長幌，寫著「孫羊店」。余輝讀作孫記正店開的羊肉分號：簷下掛著羊肺、羊腸、羊肝、羊肚，價牌上寫著「□斤六十足」。這個「足」字，是說店家要足數的錢，不收打了折扣的「省陌」。也有人把案上掛的讀作一扇豬肉。故宮名畫記又說，門口板凳上坐著個胖老闆，讓人想起《水滸傳》裏的「鎮關西」鄭屠。
landmarks.long_en: The butcher's shop on the corner hangs a long white cloth banner reading “Sun Yang Shop.” Yu Hui reads it as a lamb branch of Sun's main tavern: under the eaves hang lamb lungs, intestines, liver and tripe, and the price tag reads “[?] jin, sixty full.” That word “full” means the shopkeeper wants a full count of coins and will not take the discounted “short string.” Some read what hangs on the counter as a side of pork. The Palace Museum's notes add that the fat shopkeeper sitting on a bench at the door recalls Butcher Zheng, “Zhenguanxi,” in Water Margin.
landmarks.quote: 都市錢陌，官用七十七，街市通用七十五，魚肉菜七十二陌。
landmarks.quote_en: The city's strings of cash: official use seventy-seven to the string, general use in the streets seventy-five, fish, meat and vegetables seventy-two.
landmarks.cite: 余輝《清明上河圖深度游》・故宮名畫記・《東京夢華錄》
landmarks.cite_en: Yu Hui, An In-Depth Tour of the Qingming Scroll · Palace Museum, Minghuaji · Dreams of Splendour of the Eastern Capital
longSrc: map S6.bld.butcher_shop_sun: the long white flag 孫羊店
YH23: 孙记正店外高悬着"孙羊店"的幌子…该店的分部——羊肉铺…羊肺，还有羊肠、羊肝、羊肚…价格牌："□斤六十足"，这个"足"字，表明了店家不收"省陌"的钱贯

landmarks.name: 街頭說書
landmarks.line: 說話人說三分，聽客圍了一圈。
landmarks.line_en: The storyteller tells a tale; the listeners ring round him.
landmarks.src: 名画记 39 闹市说书; 余辉 2014 街头说书; 《东京梦华录》卷五 京瓦伎艺 '霍四究，说《三分》'
landmarks.long: 肉鋪門前，一圈人圍著一位大鬍子說書人。他面朝外，聽眾大多背對著我們，聽得入神。余輝說這是全卷唯一一處公開的表演，圍聽的有僧人、道士、讀書人，也有婦人孩子。故宮名畫記說，城市興起了廣大的市民，北宋的娛樂業跟著興盛，雜劇、唱曲、傀儡戲、講史、小說樣樣都有，還出了不少名角。
landmarks.long_en: In front of the butcher's, a circle of people gathers around a bearded storyteller. He faces outward while most of the listeners have their backs to us, absorbed. Yu Hui says this is the only public performance in the whole scroll; the crowd includes monks, Daoists, scholars, and women and children. The Palace Museum's notes say that as a mass of townspeople arose, entertainment flourished in Northern Song, with variety plays, singing, puppet shows, history telling and storytelling all on offer, and many famous performers emerged.
landmarks.quote: 霍四究，說《三分》。尹常賣，《五代史》。
landmarks.quote_en: Huo Sijiu tells the Three Kingdoms. Yin Changmai tells the History of the Five Dynasties.
landmarks.cite: 余輝《清明上河圖深度游》・故宮名畫記・《東京夢華錄》・畫中所見
landmarks.cite_en: Yu Hui, An In-Depth Tour of the Qingming Scroll · Palace Museum, Minghuaji · Dreams of Splendour of the Eastern Capital · What the painting shows

landmarks.name: 久住王員外家
landmarks.line_en: An inn; upstairs a scholar studies.
landmarks.src: 名画记 42 久住王员外家 (the painted sign); 余辉 士子苦读
landmarks.long: 街南一座兩層的客店，路邊招牌頂上兩個小字「久住」並排，下面寫著「王員外家」。故宮名畫記說，「久住」有老字號、靠得住的意思，是招徠客人的話。樓上窗裏，一位客人伏案讀書，牆上掛著字幅，桌上擺著文房用具，余輝稱這一景為「士子苦讀」。每逢科舉之年，京城住滿了進京赴考的士人；客店不但住人，也存放貨物，不少買賣就在店裏說合。
landmarks.long_en: On the south side of the street stands a two-storey inn; on the roadside sign the two small characters “Long Stay” sit side by side at the top, and below is written “Wang the Squire's House.” The Palace Museum's notes say “Long Stay” suggests an old, dependable house, a phrase to draw guests. In an upstairs window a guest bends over a desk reading, with a scroll hung on the wall and writing tools on the table, a scene Yu Hui calls “The Scholar Studying Hard.” In examination years the capital filled with scholars arriving for the exams; an inn housed not only people but also goods, and many deals were struck right in the inn.
landmarks.cite: 故宮名畫記・余輝・畫中所見
landmarks.cite_en: Palace Museum, Minghuaji · Yu Hui · What the painting shows

map S6.bld.inn_wang_yuanwai: two storeys, south side of the street; a scholar reading at a desk upstairs
MHJ 42: "久住"含有"老店"、"老字号"之意…墙上还挂着书法艺术品，桌子上陈设着文房用具…旅店不仅用来招待客人住宿，还可堆积商品，很多买卖也在这里说和

landmarks.name: 劉家香藥鋪
landmarks.line: 招牌寫著：劉家上色沉檀揀香。
landmarks.line_en: The sign reads: Liu Family, Finest Selected Aloeswood and Sandalwood.
landmarks.src: 名画记 41 香药铺; the painted sign 刘家上色沉檀拣香
landmarks.long: 十字路口斜對角是一家香鋪，門前招牌寫著「劉家上色沉檀揀香」：上等的沉香、檀香，都是揀選過的好貨。招牌最末一字被行人的帽子擋住，學者讀作「香」。故宮名畫記說，香料在宋朝的進口貨裏佔了不小的份量，海外貿易甚至被稱為「香料貿易」；香料成了茶、鹽、礬之外，替官府賺取巨利的大宗貨物，買賣也受官府管制。
landmarks.long_en: On the diagonal corner of the crossroads is an incense shop, with a sign at the door reading “Liu Family, Finest Selected Aloeswood and Sandalwood”: top-grade aloeswood and sandalwood, hand-picked goods. The last character on the sign is blocked by a passer-by's hat, and scholars read it as “incense.” The Palace Museum's notes say spices made up no small share of Song imports, so that overseas trade was even called the “spice trade”; spices, alongside tea, salt and alum, became a major source of great profit for the government, and trade in them was controlled by the state.
landmarks.cite: 故宮名畫記・畫中所見
landmarks.cite_en: Palace Museum, Minghuaji · What the painting shows
longSrc: map S6.bld.incense_shop_liu: signboard 劉家上色沉檀揀□ (last character hidden behind a hat; 香 by scholarship)
map S6.prop.signboard_liu_incense_3147
MHJ 41: 街道的对角是家香铺…香料在宋朝的进口货物中，占了相当的比例。所以宋朝的海外贸易又称为"香料贸易"…成了茶、盐、矾之外，为政府获得巨额利润的大宗商品。它的销售也受官府的控制

landmarks.name: 「解」字招牌
landmarks.line: 士子圍著老者，打聽科場消息。
landmarks.line_en: Scholars gather round an old man, asking about the exams.
landmarks.src: 名画记 45 '解'字招牌 (an office for candidates' formalities); disputed: 余辉 2014 考前求解 (a fortune-teller)
landmarks.long: 十字街西南角，一塊招牌斜倚簷下，上面掛著一個「解」字，竹棚裏一群穿儒生衣冠的年輕人，圍著一位老者或坐或立。這個「解」字怎麼讀，說法不一：故宮以為科舉與「解」字關係密切，這是替舉子辦理應考手續的地方，年輕人是來打聽考試消息的；余輝讀作算命鋪，舉子們在考前求問前程，並把這裏列為結尾「三問」中的問命；香港的教材則說它是當鋪。這裏取故宮之說。
landmarks.long_en: At the south-west corner of the crossroads a sign leans under the eaves bearing the single character “Jie,” and inside a bamboo shed a group of young men in scholars' dress sit or stand around an old man. How to read “Jie” is disputed: the Palace Museum holds that the character is closely tied to the civil-service examinations, that this is a place that handles applications for candidates, and that the young men are asking for exam news; Yu Hui reads it as a fortune-teller's shop, where candidates ask about their prospects before the exam, and lists it as the question about fate among the closing “three questions”; a Hong Kong textbook says it is a pawnshop. Here we take the Palace Museum's reading.
landmarks.cite: 故宮名畫記・余輝〈最後三問〉・畫中所見
landmarks.cite_en: Palace Museum, Minghuaji · Yu Hui, The Last Three Questions · What the painting shows
longSrc: map S6.prop.jie_signboard_2085 (tall signboard leaning against the eave, plaque 解); S6.grp.jie_ring (young men in a ring round a seated man; a hooded old man)

landmarks.name: 方井
landmarks.line: 井口架成田字，四人可同時汲水。
landmarks.line_en: The well-mouth is framed like the character “field,” so four can draw at once.
landmarks.long: 十字街西頭的水井邊，幾個人正在打水：一個站在井架上拉著井繩，一個彎腰把水桶提上來，一個把滿桶扛上肩頭。井口用木樑架成「田」字，故宮名畫記說這樣可以幾個人同時打水，又說這口井並不深；余輝則說這是富人街坊的官井，井口架上橫樑，是怕人失足落井。這麼大的京城，吃水用水本是一件大事。
landmarks.long_en: At the well at the west end of the crossroads, several people are drawing water: one stands on the well frame hauling the rope, one bends to lift up the bucket, and one swings a full bucket onto his shoulder. The well-mouth is framed with timber beams in the shape of the character “field,” which the Palace Museum's notes say lets several people draw water at once, adding that the well is not deep; Yu Hui says instead that this is the official well of a wealthy neighbourhood, and that crossbeams were put over the mouth so no one would fall in. In so large a capital, getting water was a matter of real importance.
landmarks.cite: 故宮名畫記・余輝《清明上河圖深度游》・畫中所見
landmarks.cite_en: Palace Museum, Minghuaji · Yu Hui, An In-Depth Tour of the Qingming Scroll · What the painting shows
